# Answer — generator-shortcuts

**Question:** For this generator, name the strongest plausible shortcut or rival
rule that fits the canonical demonstrations. Give an exact input on which it
disagrees with the intended rule, how you checked the output, and whether your
proposed generator emits such cases.

## Rival and why it matters

Use the **numeric predecessor of each region's foreground color**, cyclically
within the sorted three-color foreground palette, to fill that region's holes.
Do not use the next region's spatial position. Keep existing foreground and
full-background separator columns unchanged.

This rival fits 6/6 usable canonical pairs (three unique inputs) and 600/600
baseline generated samples, because the baseline excludes every ascending
numeric color cycle. With three distinct colors, all remaining cyclic orders
are descending, so numeric predecessor equals spatial next on that restricted
support. The fixed-2/2/2-boundary rival is weaker: it fits only 4/6 canonical
pairs. No claim of a unique strongest rival among all possible programs is made.

## Exact generated counterexample

Final task `19e04051ad0d`, version `3.1.0`, generator SHA-256
`769ab701b32aa455b835a1154b7b7a528cb34fa93cf2f1328eab3072ad892a4d`. Seed **600123**, sample index **0**, difficulty
**easy**, no overrides. Each line below is one row of integer ARC colors:

```text
7303323
7300333
3330332
7303322
7300323
3330322
7330332
7300323
3303322
7330333
```

Background is 3. Full-background columns are 1 and 4 (zero-based). Region
widths are 1,2,2 and foreground colors from left to right are **7,0,2**. The
intended replacement map is 7->0, 0->2, 2->7; the numeric predecessor map on
sorted palette [0,2,7] is 7->2, 0->7, 2->0.

For example, the hole at row 0/column 3 must become **2**; the rival makes it
**7**. The same disagreement repeats across all region holes, so this is not an
implementation-boundary ambiguity.

## Verification and support

The input passes the strict input validator and is emitted ordinarily by the
final generator. `checks/color-cycle-final.json` retains its exact generation
arguments and diagnostic output. The output was independently obtained with:

```sh
python3 run_with_racket.py python3 -m arcpuzzles apply 19e04051ad0d --input ../checks/counterexample/input.json --out ../checks/counterexample/racket.json
```

Command cwd: packet root; effective cwd: `/mnt/data/arc_review_222344/repo`;
exit 0. Executed RULE_HASH is `3448ae999e2e`. The CLI's exact
source/input/output hashes, complete input, actual output and rival output are
combined in `checks/counterexample/counterexample.json`. Racket agrees with the
Python diagnostic mirror on this input; Racket remains the authority.

The final generator includes both cycle orientations rather than excluding
this counterexample family. In the source-bound seed-600123 probe, indexes
0..199 per band, this rival fits 300/600 individual inputs but survives 0/594
overlapping three-demo windows. Every production-census lesson and all four
query placements per lesson refute it across 300 lessons/1,200 unique inputs.
This is measured support against declared rivals, not proof that every possible
learner or arbitrary subset of examples will infer the intended rule.
